draft.summary: The food delivery market in Nepal shows modest growth driven by smartphone adoption and pandemic‑induced demand, but the evidence is thin and lacks quantitative market‑size data. Foodmandu is the largest platform with over 500,000 users and recent Series B funding, while commission rates vary across providers. Competition is intense and delivery inefficiencies remain a challenge.

competitors.name: Foodmandu
competitors.note: Over 500,000 registered users and a Series B round that gave Team Ventures a 20% stake [F3][F4].

competitors.name: Foodbusters
competitors.note: Charges restaurants a commission of about 14‑15% [F1].

key_observations: Commission fees differ: Foodbusters 14‑15%, Foodmandu ~22%, Bhoj ~20%, Pathao Food ~18% [F1].
Foodmandu has over 500,000 registered users and supports QR, digital wallets, cards and cash on delivery [F3].
The COVID‑19 pandemic accelerated food‑delivery activity in Kathmandu, prompting many restaurants to partner with platforms [F5].
Growth is driven by rising smartphone penetration and changing lifestyles, but delivery inefficiencies and intense competition are key challenges [F6][F7].
Foodmandu's market success has spurred entry of several other food‑delivery startups in Nepal [F8].
